entries.title: OpenAI Computer History Feature Brings Keystroke Logging and Prompt Injection Risk Into Enterprise Scope
entries.summary: OpenAI's new opt-in Computer History feature for ChatGPT Pro/Business/Enterprise records keystrokes, clicks, and app context to build AI memories, stores interaction data locally unencrypted for up to 48 hours before server transmission, and is blocked in the EEA, UK, and Switzerland — surfacing enterprise-grade prompt-injection and data-retention governance gaps.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: OpenAI Computer History feature brings keylogging and prompt injection into enterprise scope

entries.title: Google Releases Gemini 3.7 Flash With CBRN/Cyber-Offense Safeguards; Always-On Gemini Spark Agent Raises Agentic Oversight Gaps
entries.summary: Google released Gemini 3.7 Flash on August 13 with updated frontier safety measures covering CBRN and cyber-offense misuse alongside a published model card, but the model also powers Gemini Spark — an autonomous agent that operates continuously on behalf of users across Google Workspace — raising material questions about human oversight controls in always-on agentic deployments.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: Gemini 3.7 Flash adds CBRN safeguards but its always-on agent raises oversight gaps

entries.title: Apple Registers Custom AI Model With China's CAC via Alibaba Partnership — First US Company to Obtain Proprietary AI Approval in China
entries.summary: Apple developed a custom LLM for the Chinese market in collaboration with Alibaba and registered it with China's Cyberspace Administration ahead of a planned Apple Intelligence rollout, making Apple the first US company to have a proprietary AI model government-cleared for deployment in China and setting a compliance template for foreign AI firms operating under China's mandatory model registration regime.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: Apple's China AI model sets a compliance precedent for foreign firms

entries.title: arXiv 2608.12880: MCP Agent Security Evaluations Show Treatment Leakage — 58 Historical ATTACK_SUCCESS Labels Revised to Authorized Benign
entries.summary: An audit of a published MCP agent security evaluation campaign finds that treatment metadata directly gated the ATTACK_SUCCESS label, so fixed behavior could flip class under treatment relabeling; a treatment-blind reconstruction corrects 58 ATTACK_SUCCESS or HIJACK_ATTEMPT records to authorized benign completions, with only three verified protected-data transfers remaining — a concrete reminder that label-based security benchmarks require construct-validity checks before any attack-rate claim is trusted.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.12996 (ATOBench): New Benchmark Makes Autonomous Pentest Agent Verification Behavior Observable Against Deceptive Targets
entries.summary: ATOBench injects registered response transformations at runtime in autonomous penetration-testing agent episodes and pairs each with a native episode to expose how agents handle deceptive or lying target evidence, finding that increased agent activity can mask a broken verification chain — a process-level evaluation lens that matters for assessing whether AI-driven offensive security tools are actually reasoning about evidence or just hallucinating conclusions.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.13030 (InterSAGE): Trust-Native Protocol Suite Addresses Missing Security Substrate for Multi-Agent Interoperability
entries.summary: InterSAGE proposes a four-layer trust protocol (Persistent Identity, Discovery, Trust Negotiation, Accountability) for multi-agent systems that complements existing communication protocols like MCP and A2A by binding developer, code package, operator, and deployment context to agent identities and enforcing capability attenuation and kernel-mediated cryptographic audit trails — closing identity spoofing, unauthorized delegation, and audit-evasion gaps that no prior architecture jointly addresses.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.12962 (BVBench): Vertical Federated Learning Backdoor Research-Practice Gap — Near-Perfect Attack Rates Collapse Under Realistic Constraints
entries.summary: A practice-oriented systematic study of backdoor vulnerabilities in Vertical Federated Learning finds that prior work's near-perfect attack success rates and proposed defenses fail to hold under realistic conditions because existing approaches rely on unrealistic prior knowledge, and poorly designed evaluation practices have kept this gap hidden; BVBench provides a fair, practical benchmark revealing the field's understanding of VFL backdoor risk is fragile.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.12623: Black-Box Backdoor Detection in LM Classifiers via 'Groundedness Drift' — No Trigger Knowledge Required
entries.summary: Groundedness Drift, a lightweight score measuring whether a classifier's answer summary remains grounded in its input, achieves higher AUROC and lower residual attack success rate than all compared detectors at a 5% clean false-positive rate budget across five attack families and two 7B backbones using only clean calibration data and explanation rationales — offering a practical black-box audit for backdoored classifiers when neither the trigger nor training data is available.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.12444: Decision-Contract Theory Closes the All-Abstain Loophole in AI Security Risk Certificates
entries.summary: Any risk certificate that does not specify which inputs the system acts on and what 'correct' means can be trivially satisfied by a system that never acts; this paper formalizes a non-degenerate actionability certificate that excludes all-abstain solutions by construction, instantiated on ATT&CK-aligned LLM alert triage across six models where false-attribution risk stays at or below target in 90.3% of configurations — directly relevant to designing auditable AI security decision systems.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.13304 (WIFA): Intent-Based Safety Tuning Reduces Over-Refusal of Wrapped Harmful Prompts From 25.7% to 17.4%
entries.summary: Wrapper-Based Intent-Form Augmentation automatically pairs wrapped harmful training examples with structurally matched wrapped benign counterexamples, enabling safety fine-tuning to target underlying intent rather than surface form; on Qwen, WIFA-Boost maximizes refusal of transformed-harmful prompts while A-GCRT (Anchored Group-Consistent Refusal Training) reduces OR-Bench over-refusal from 25.7% to 17.4%, without requiring an external teacher model.

entries.title: D'Addario Reverses 14-Day AI Denial Then Commits to Mandatory Disclosure — Case Study in Missing Pre-Publication Governance Gate
entries.summary: Guitar accessories company D'Addario confirmed it used Suno to generate audio in a promotional video after nearly two weeks of public denials, also acknowledged suppressing critical social media comments, then committed to mandatory AI disclosure requirements for employees and creative partners — illustrating how the absence of a pre-publication AI review gate converts undisclosed AI use into compounding reputational and regulatory exposure.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: D'Addario's two-week AI denial exposes the missing disclosure gate in marketing governance
